data.current_description:
A lead consists of two fieldlists:
- prospect: A person or company along with contact information.
- interest: The formulated interest of the prospect.

A fieldlist is a collection of fields with an optional ordering, where each field consists of
- an identifier - the name of the field,
- a type, which describes syntax and semantic of the value,
- the value of the field, which is a string-representation conforming to the given type.

The field types are segmented in two classes:
- generic types, which only describe the syntax of the value (e.g. 'text:singleline' or 'number:natural')
- specific types, which additionally specify a semantic, on how to interpret the value (e.g. 'text:multiline:address')
data.description_suggestion: Creates a new lead with prospect and interest fieldlists. Each fieldlist contains fields with identifiers, types (generic or specific), and string values. Generic types describe syntax (e.g., 'text:singleline', 'number:natural'), while specific types add semantic meaning (e.g., 'text:multiline:address'). Returns the created lead object with assigned leadId. The lead becomes owned by the creating company and is available for distribution to sales partners.

data.current_description:
Use this operation to retrieve lists of leads that your company owns.\
The owner of a lead is the creator of it.

### Continuation
The amount of leads you can retrieve by a single request is limited.
You can iterate through all your leads using a continuation token which you get with every response header.
Use your previous query and add the returned continuation token to get the next set of results.
Once you get an empty result you know that there are no more leads available.

### Sorting
You may sort the results according to some sorting criteria in ascending or descending order.
You can also sort by multiple fields.

### Filtering
You may filter you list by some filter criteria.
The most common use case is to filter by modified leads since the last time you fetched modified leads. (Incremental updates)
- Example: GET /leads?modifiedAt=gte:2022-06-01

### FieldLists
By default this operation returns meta data and transactional data of leads.
So you will be able to tell when some lead has been modified as well as whether a lead has been won/lost or ist still in progress.\
If you are interested in the field lists of your leads as well, use the "includeFieldLists" query parameter!

### Commissions
A lead can be processed more than once — by several sales partners in turn or, with multi distribution, at the same time.
Every item carries the **newest** processing (by startedAt) as the flat "commission" object, exactly as before,
and additionally **all** processings of the lead as the "commissions" array, newest first, each element shaped like "commission".\
A lead that has never been processed has no "commission" and an empty "commissions" array.\
The array is additive and is being rolled out stage by stage; where it is not available yet, the field is absent.
Integrations that only read "commission" keep working unchanged.
data.summary_suggestion: Retrieve paginated list of owned leads with filtering and sorting
data.description_suggestion: Retrieves a paginated list of leads owned by your company (created by your company). Supports continuation tokens for iterating through large result sets. Supports sorting by multiple fields in ascending or descending order, and filtering by criteria such as modifiedAt for incremental updates (e.g., modifiedAt=gte:2022-06-01). By default returns metadata and transactional data (modification timestamps, status: won/lost/in-progress). Use includeFieldLists parameter to include prospect and interest fieldlists. Each lead includes the newest commission (processing by a sales partner) as a flat object, plus a commissions array with all historical processings ordered by startedAt (newest first). Leads never processed have no commission field and an empty commissions array.

data.current_description:
A lead consists of two fieldlists:
- prospect: A person or company along with contact information.
- interest: The formulated interest of the prospect.

A fieldlist is a collection of fields with an optional ordering, where each field consists of
- an identifier - the name of the field,
- a type, which describes syntax and semantic of the value,
- the value of the field, which is a string-representation conforming to the given type.

The field types are segmented in two classes:
- generic types, which only describe the syntax of the value (e.g. 'text:singleline' or 'number:natural')
- specific types, which additionally specify a semantic, on how to interpret the value (e.g. 'text:multiline:address')
data.description_suggestion: Creates a new lead with prospect and interest fieldlists. Each fieldlist contains fields with identifiers, types (generic or specific), and string values. Generic types describe syntax (e.g., 'text:singleline', 'number:natural'), while specific types add semantic meaning (e.g., 'text:multiline:address'). Returns the created lead object with assigned leadId. The lead becomes owned by the creating company and is available for distribution to sales partners.
data.reasoning: Description explains lead structure well but lacks information about what the operation returns (the created lead object with ID) and side effects (lead ownership and availability). Added these details for complete AI agent understanding of the operation's outcome.

### Continuation
The amount of leads you can retrieve by a single request is limited.
You can iterate through all your leads using a continuation token which you get with every response header.
Use your previous query and add the returned continuation token to get the next set of results.
Once you get an empty result you know that there are no more leads available.

### Sorting
You may sort the results according to some sorting criteria in ascending or descending order.
You can also sort by multiple fields.

### Filtering
You may filter you list by some filter criteria.
The most common use case is to filter by modified leads since the last time you fetched modified leads. (Incremental updates)
- Example: GET /leads?modifiedAt=gte:2022-06-01

### FieldLists
By default this operation returns meta data and transactional data of leads.
So you will be able to tell when some lead has been modified as well as whether a lead has been won/lost or ist still in progress.\
If you are interested in the field lists of your leads as well, use the "includeFieldLists" query parameter!

### Commissions
A lead can be processed more than once — by several sales partners in turn or, with multi distribution, at the same time.
Every item carries the **newest** processing (by startedAt) as the flat "commission" object, exactly as before,
and additionally **all** processings of the lead as the "commissions" array, newest first, each element shaped like "commission".\
A lead that has never been processed has no "commission" and an empty "commissions" array.\
The array is additive and is being rolled out stage by stage; where it is not available yet, the field is absent.
Integrations that only read "commission" keep working unchanged.

Supports sorting by multiple fields in ascending or descending order, and filtering by criteria such as modifiedAt for incremental updates (e.g., modifiedAt=gte:2022-06-01). By default returns metadata and transactional data (modification timestamps, status: won/lost/in-progress). Use includeFieldLists parameter to include prospect and interest fieldlists. Each lead includes the newest commission (processing by a sales partner) as a flat object, plus a commissions array with all historical processings ordered by startedAt (newest first). Leads never processed have no commission field and an empty commissions array.
